question: A 67-year-old man comes to the emergency department for evaluation of progressively worsening edema and decreased urine output over the past few days. He has a history of chronic sinus infections and was hospitalized last year for a suspected pneumonia with hemoptysis. Physical exam shows bilateral pitting edema of the lower extremities. Serum studies show a creatinine of 3.4 mg/dL and blood urea nitrogen of 35 mg/dL. Urine dipstick shows 3+ blood. A kidney biopsy is performed and light microscopy shows crescent-shaped glomeruli. Immunofluorescent microscopy of the tissue sample is most likely to show which of the following findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Crescent-shaped glomeruli on light microscopy" -> "Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN)" -> "Immunofluorescent microscopy likely to show subepithelial deposits" -> 95% CHAIN: "Crescent-shaped glomeruli on light microscopy" -> "RPGN" -> "Immunofluorescent microscopy likely to show subendothelial deposits" -> 80% CHAIN: "Crescent-shaped glomeruli on light microscopy" -> "RPGN" -> "Immunofluorescent microscopy likely to show intramembranous deposits" -> 95%
analysis: The patient's presentation with worsening edema, decreased urine output, elevated creatinine and BUN, along with crescent-shaped glomeruli on kidney biopsy, is suggestive of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN). In RPGN, immunofluorescent microscopy typically shows pauci-immune findings, meaning minimal or no immune deposits. This is in contrast to other types of glomerulonephritis where immune deposits are usually present.
